doc.title: Catherine Russell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 26, 2018

title: Learning what a gig is: mother's working life
summary: Russell recalls her mother taking her bass to work and choral rehearsals, and friends not believing musicians' work or her Louis Armstrong connection.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When you were a kid, can you recall when you learned what the word “gig” meant?

Probably when my mother, you know, because my parents were — well my dad was home a lot at that point. That was towards the end of his life. But my mother didn’t stop working. So people would call the house and call her for work and she’d go to work. She’d take her bass and she’d go to work, or she was also a concert choral singer so she would go to choral rehearsals. So I would know that that was where she was going. That’s what she did.
And was there was a point where, in talking to your friends, that you discovered that what your mom did was a little different?
